authority: Pravidlá slovenského pravopisu, chapter V; project transcription in docs/pravidla-delenia-slov.md
scope: All 144 manual-vs-engine conflicts observed before or during the 2026-08-24 reconciliation cycle.

policy.human_matches_psp: The stored human result matches the applicable PSP rule; the engine must change.
policy.engine_matches_psp: The current engine result matches the applicable PSP rule; the human annotation must not be used as gold.
policy.neither_matches_psp: Neither stored human nor current engine output matches the applicable PSP result; both require correction.
policy.both_psp_different_modes: Both point sets are PSP-permitted, but one is preferred and the other belongs to the permissive/contextual mode.
policy.psp_requires_pronunciation: PSP requires the actual pronunciation or lexical identity of a foreign form; neither voice is adjudicated without that evidence.

groups.reason: The human review identifies a real prefix, compound, inflectional seam, hiatus, or foreign graphic unit that the engine missed or falsely reanalysed.
The manual result uses a phonological onset instead of the PSP consonant-count rule, invents a false seam, splits one pronounced vowel group, or omits another preferred point.

JÚĽŠ analyzes aeronaut as aero- + -naut. The preferred break is aero|nauti and the foreign one-syllable graphic group au in -naut- must stay intact; at adjudication both stored Human and Engine split it as na|uti and omitted the compound seam. The approved Human and algorithmic corrections now implement the adjudicated result.

The engine keeps the preferred compound seam before the vowel-initial second member; the human review additionally offers the contextual point that pulls that vowel left. The preferred and permissive files must therefore differ.

The human point preserves the perceived po- + sled + -ný morphemic structure; the engine point applies syllabic division across sl. PSP permits the syllabic reading when the morphemic structure is not perceived, so neither result invalidates the other.

The form is foreign, a proper name, Latin, or textually ambiguous. PSP does not permit deriving its indivisible letter groups and hiatuses from spelling alone. A cited pronunciation or lexical source is required before either stored output becomes gold.
